clue.text: Instant cut-back

parts.note: to cut something is to split it
to back someone is to second or support them

explanation.surface: A sharp order to trim something back right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads as part of 'cut-back' but is a verb on its own: to support a motion is to second it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fraction of time, a moment, is called an instant.

clue.text: Governors once a bit reflective on board

indicators.note: 'on board' is read as being aboard a ship, so the ship's letters go around the rest

parts.note: a ship one goes on board is a steamship, abbreviated SS

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the word for bit is read in reverse

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A rather thoughtful board meeting, where former governors sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship); 'reflective' turns PART into TRAP after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Satraps were provincial rulers in ancient Persia, hence governors of old.

clue.text: A city story about the fifties

indicators.note: the word for story goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a story is a fib, a lie
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties make LL

explanation.surface: A town's tale set in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fifties' looks like a decade but means two Roman fifties, L and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France.

clue.text: The fatigue of residents after moving

indicators.note: once moved about, the letters of the word residents are rearranged

explanation.surface: Householders are worn out after a house move.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue is weariness, the state of being worn out.

clue.text: A bird in danger nearly extinct

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the run of letters across danger nearly

explanation.surface: A bird species under threat and close to dying out.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Viewed too much, so must be supervised

explanation.surface: Something watched too often needs a minder.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as OVER-SEEN it means seen to excess; as one word it means watched over.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen to excess and, as a single word, managed or watched over by a boss.

clue.text: Man writing poetry finished about noon

indicators.note: the word for finished wraps about the letter for noon

parts.note: finished means done

explanation.surface: A poet wraps up his verse around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a seventeenth-century English poet, a man who wrote verse.

clue.text: Many twist over the French contract

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for twist sits over, above, the French article

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, so many
to twist is to wind
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Lots of people revise the French agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun (agreement) but is the verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or diminish gradually.

clue.text: Even but scant-not freely available

indicators.note: letters made freely available are loose to be rearranged, here those of scant-not

explanation.surface: Steady, yet hardly ever on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Even here means steady, unchanging, uniform.

clue.text: Spreading on treacle allowed variation

indicators.note: spreading the letters of on treacle rearranges them

explanation.surface: How much syrup you can spread is a matter of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineering tolerance is the permitted deviation from a measurement.

clue.text: Ruthless she certainly was not!

parts.note: in the Bible Ruth stayed loyally with her mother-in-law, so this woman was never without Ruth

explanation.surface: A woman praised as anything but cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruthless' means cruel on the surface; split it as 'Ruth-less', lacking Ruth, the daughter-in-law who refused to leave her.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, the widow whose daughter-in-law Ruth vowed to go wherever she went.

clue.text: Changes as the afternoon begins

explanation.surface: Plans shift once lunchtime arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM ENDS: the morning (a.m.) finishes as the afternoon starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends are alterations to a text; split, the morning stops exactly when the afternoon starts.

clue.text: Disparaged article by new press editor

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a new version of the word press has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper item put out by the editor rubbished someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to slander or run down someone's reputation.

clue.text: A member of the family in hospital?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a relative is a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sibling, and also a senior ward nurse in British hospitals.

clue.text: Sol airs various odd items

parts.note: Sol is the Roman sun god, so the sun
to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: The sun dries out a miscellany of bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small articles not worth listing separately.

clue.text: Maybe a rep used influence

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version, so the letters of a rep used are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps a salesman leaned on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence someone is to win them over by argument.

clue.text: Consumers of this may well get all wound up

definitions.text: Consumers of this may well get all wound up

parts.words: Consumers of this may well get all wound up
parts.note: eaters of this long pasta twirl it round their forks, so it is the food that ends up wound, not the diners

explanation.surface: Something that makes people who use it agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' suggests annoyed diners; really the strands are wound round a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strands of pasta that diners twirl around a fork.

clue.text: "Disgusted" was up in arms

explanation.surface: Sickened people rose in rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Repelled or sickened, and also having risen in rebellion against authority.

clue.text: Left, and that's ominous!

explanation.surface: A remark that going left bodes ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, and the left side was thought unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic term for the left-hand side, and also threatening or menacing.

clue.text: Making great efforts to get pound in discount

indicators.note: the pound sign goes in the word for discount

parts.note: a discount is a saving
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Working hard to get a pound off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiling or labouring hard, like a slave.

clue.text: Delay retirement

parts.note: retirement here means going to bed for the night, and putting that off to stay awake for someone

explanation.surface: Putting off giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving a job; here it means retiring to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay out of bed until someone comes home.

clue.text: The lady will see news men around mid-week

indicators.note: the word for news men goes around the middle letters

parts.note: the press is a collective term for journalists

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word week

explanation.surface: A woman will see reporters in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a title in the nobility, such as a duchess or countess.

clue.text: Wear a piece of underwear is put back on

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear

indicators.note: the word is is put back, written backwards

explanation.surface: A bra is put back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear' looks like a verb to do with clothing; it is the noun, erosion by rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasion is damage caused by friction or rubbing, wear and tear.

clue.text: Being confused, loves to find an answer

indicators.note: the letters of loves are confused, mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone muddled by love trying to work things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve is to work out the answer to a problem.

clue.text: Novelty trade

explanation.surface: Selling new gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change was the old term for an exchange where merchants traded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something different for variety, and an exchange or swap of goods.

clue.text: Count maybe as currency no longer

explanation.surface: Perhaps an aristocrat is no longer rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The noble was an old English gold coin of the fourteenth to sixteenth centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is an example of an aristocrat, and the noble was an old English coin.

clue.text: Engineers fix up running water in Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue reading up reverses the letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to fix something is to do it, as in do up

explanation.surface: Engineers repair waterworks in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river on the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming much of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Exemplary though singular business arrangement

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun
a deal is a business agreement

explanation.surface: A model business agreement for a single party.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect, serving as a model to copy.

clue.text: A record of ups and downs in the main

definitions.text: A record of ups and downs in the main

parts.words: A record of ups and downs in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, so a list of the rising and falling sea level through the day

explanation.surface: A chart showing life's fortunes overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' seems to mean mostly; the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A published list of times of high and low water at a harbour.

clue.text: Bands in trees showing age

indicators.note: the word for bands goes in the word for trees

parts.note: elders are small trees with white flowers and dark berries
bands are stripes or lines

explanation.surface: Rings in tree trunks reveal how old they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Being elderly, the state of advanced years.
